Note::collapse_whitespace¶

Back to Note API Reference

Signature¶

Note Note::collapse_whitespace() const

Trim And Fold Every Run Of Whitespace To One Space¶

collapse_whitespace() returns a new Note, same shape as the input, in which each cell has its leading and trailing whitespace removed and every interior run of one or more whitespace characters replaced by a single space. It is the one-call “tidy the spacing” step for text pulled from HTML, PDFs, wrapped source, or copy-paste.

Whitespace is the ASCII set space, \t, \n, \r, \f, \v. A tab becomes a space; a run of blank lines becomes a single space, so multi-line content is flattened to one line — use collapse_newlines instead when line breaks must survive, or dedent to strip only common indentation.

collapse_whitespace changes only spacing — no letters, punctuation, or non-ASCII are touched. It is shape-preserving, cell-independent, and returns a fresh Note.

Example 1: A Batch¶

std::cout << pluss::note::print(
    pluss::make_note({"  hello   world  ", "a\t\tb\nc", "clean"}).collapse_whitespace())
    << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, encoding=utf8)
["hello world", "a b c", "clean"]

The doubled internal spaces, the tabs, and the newline all collapse to one space each; the ends are trimmed.

Example 2: Shape Is Preserved¶

const pluss::Note n = pluss::make_note({{"  a  b  ", " c "}}).collapse_whitespace();
std::cout << n << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[1, 2], dim=2, numel=2, encoding=utf8)
[
  ["a b", "c"]
]

See Also¶

  • Note::collapse_spaces: fold space/tab runs but leave newlines and the cell edges alone.

  • Note::collapse_newlines: fold only runs of line breaks.

  • Note::strip: trim the edges without touching interior spacing.
